name: Lafayette
seo_title: Christmas Events for Kids in Lafayette, CA 2026
seo_desc: Kids' Christmas in Lafayette, CA: free Lafayette Express train rides, Santa and tree lighting in the Plaza, plus a holiday panto at Town Hall Theatre.
lede: Lafayette keeps Christmas simple and local: one big free evening in Lafayette Plaza with Santa, a holiday train and the tree lighting, followed by a family panto at Town Hall Theatre.
celebrates: The Lafayette Chamber of Commerce leads the season with It's a Wonderful Life in Lafayette Holiday Celebration in Lafayette Plaza, at the corner of Mt. Diablo Boulevard and Moraga Road. Santa arrives, the Lafayette Express holiday train gives rides, the official tree is lit and local groups perform. The chamber lists the evening as a free community event. Town Hall Theatre Company stages a holiday panto each December on School Street, and downtown Lafayette glows with twinkle lights sponsored by local businesses and the City of Lafayette.
lastyear: In 2025 the Lafayette Chamber held the celebration on Sunday, December 7. Its recap describes families enjoying Santa photos, train rides on the Lafayette Express, the official tree lighting, live performances from local groups, kids' activities and holiday treats. East Bay Nursery supplied the tree and Light It Up provided the lights. In 2024 Santa paraded along Golden Gate Way from First Street and reached Lafayette Plaza at about 4:30 pm.
facts: Lafayette is named for the Marquis de Lafayette, the French officer who fought in the American Revolutionary War. The community was founded in 1857, and it incorporated as a city on July 29, 1968. Lafayette Reservoir sits in the southwestern part of town. The chamber's holiday event also features Old Betsy, a firetruck brought out by the Lafayette Historical Society for photos with Santa.
trains: Lafayette has its own station on the BART system, so families can ride into San Francisco or across the East Bay. Trains are also part of the town's Christmas, because the chamber's holiday celebration includes free rides on the Lafayette Express. If your family loves model trains, the Walnut Creek Model Railroad Society, a short drive away, opens its layout for a holiday train show over the weekend after Thanksgiving.
traditions: Santa arrives at Lafayette Plaza and families can visit him for free.
Free holiday train rides during the chamber's celebration.
The Plaza tree is lit during the evening, with live music from local groups.
A photo op with Santa on the historic firetruck, brought out by the Lafayette Historical Society.
Town Hall Theatre Company's family panto at 3535 School Street.
Downtown Lafayette's holiday lights, sponsored by local businesses and the City.
kidfact: The Lafayette Express is the town's holiday train, and Lafayette itself is named for a French hero of the American Revolution.
faq: What is the biggest Christmas event in Lafayette?

It's a Wonderful Life in Lafayette Holiday Celebration, presented by the Lafayette Chamber of Commerce in Lafayette Plaza. It has a free visit with Santa, free Lafayette Express train rides, the official tree lighting, live music, crafts and holiday treats.
Are there train rides in Lafayette at Christmas?

Yes. The chamber's holiday celebration offers free rides on the Lafayette Express, a holiday train, alongside Santa, photo ops and the tree lighting. The chamber says to arrive early to see Santa's arrival and suggests families plan to stay in downtown Lafayette for dinner after the event.
Where do families gather for the tree lighting?

Lafayette Plaza, at the corner of Mt. Diablo Boulevard and Moraga Road. The chamber's page lists the address as 3530 Plaza Way. The celebration includes Santa, free train rides, photo ops, live music and crafts, with the tree lighting as the centerpiece of the evening.
Is there a Christmas play for kids in Lafayette?

Town Hall Theatre Company puts on a holiday panto at its theatre at 3535 School Street. The company describes the show as a hilarious, heartwarming celebration for all ages, with pop songs, slapstick comedy and audience participation, so children are expected to cheer the heroes and boo the baddies.
How do I get to Lafayette without a car?

Lafayette has its own station on the BART system, so families can ride in from San Francisco and other Bay Area cities without a car. Check the BART schedule for the holiday weekends, and plan to walk or take a short ride from the station to the downtown plaza.
